Subject: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU mix question (RFP Q3)

Hi Irene,

We're working through the RFP responses for our Q3 generative AI pilot and want to lock the dedicated GPU commit numbers. Two asks from procurement and infra:

1) Can you provide a concise perf/$ comparison (tokens/sec per $) across A100-40GB, H100-80GB, and L40s for a mixed workload (50% short-chat, 30% medium-context, 20% long-context inference)?
2) What are Redwood's standard concessions for a 12-month reserved commit (monthly v. annual billing) at the 100–500 GPU equivalent range? Our procurement team will need clear discount bands and what throughput SLAs (p50/p95) you can guarantee for a dedicated pool.

Attached is the RFP excerpt and expected QPS profile. Please do not hesitate to call if clarifying details help — we're aiming to finalize vendor short-list next week.

Thanks,
Matthew
Senior Cloud Architect
BrightBank

Matthew — thanks for the RFP excerpt. High level answers below; I attached a simple cost model (redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx) that maps our throughput SLOs to commit tiers so your procurement team can toggle assumptions.

High-level perf/$ guidance (mixed workload you described):
- L40s (48GB): best raw perf/$ for short-chat and embedding-heavy steady QPS due to lower per-hour cost; starts to lose on long-context when memory is the dominant factor.
- A100 (40GB): strong middle ground for medium-context tasks with good throughput for batched workloads; mature quantization path but higher perf penalty for very long contexts vs H100.
- H100 (80GB): strongest for long-context models and highest single-request perf at scale, but highest list price — delivers best perf/$ only when you need large memory + high single-request throughput (e.g., >2k token generations at p95).

Key notes in the spreadsheet:
- We model token throughput/kgpu-hour across an ensemble of Llama-2-like and instruction-tuned models. The sheet has pivot slices for 50/30/20 workload.
- For your QPS profile, a 200-GPU equivalent commit split (60% L40s / 30% A100 / 10% H100) provided the most predictable cost curve in our sims; shifting to 40/40/20 improves p95 tail but increases unit cost ~8–10%.

Concessions:
- Standard committed discount bands (list): 10% @ 12-month 100-GPU equiv, 18% @ 12-month 250-GPU equiv, 25% @ 12-month 500-GPU equiv. Annual billing vs monthly gives additional 3% on top of the band.
- Throughput SLAs: 95% of requests served within target latency for pinned pool sizes (we define p50/p95 in the SOW). For 200-GPU equiv pool we can commit to p95 latency target for the workload slices listed; we include overflow bursting to hosted capacity with a cost-based fallback clause.

I'm looping Rishi to propose formal language and potential concession levers (one-off credits, initial onboarding EPUs, guardrails for bursting).

Best,
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Matthew / Irene — adding tactical options from pricing and product to make the proposal procurement-ready. Below are concrete alternatives we typically offer — choose one wick that matches BrightBank's risk profile:

Option A — Cost-minimized (preferred by infra teams)
- GPU mix: 70% L40s / 30% A100; 0% H100.
- Commit: 12-month, monthly payments.
- Discount: 18% band at 200-GPU equiv. No annual prepay uplift.
- SLA: p95 latency target for bulk traffic; no hard p95 for the rare long-context heavy tail (we provide a documented fallback to H100 on burst with transparent price multipliers).
- Tradeoff: best unit economics; p95 for long-context not guaranteed.

Option B — Latency-tail focused (preferred by product teams)
- GPU mix: 50% L40s / 30% A100 / 20% H100.
- Commit: 12-month, annual prepay recommended.
- Discount: 22% band at 200-GPU equiv + 3% annual-prepay uplift = 25% effective.
- SLA: firm p95 latency target across workload slices with dedicated H100 capacity to handle long-context tail. We include 10% burst buffer at market rate; additional burst steps negotiable.

Option C — Hybrid phased approach (recommended for pilots)
- Month 0–3: smaller commit (100-GPU equiv) to validate. Redwood provides a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of expected monthly spend for the first two months.
- Month 4–12: scale to target commit (200–300 GPU equiv) with movement in discount band depending on final size.

Concessions and legal notes:
- We can include an express credit for missed SLAs tied to monthly usage at p95 breach (capped at 10% monthly invoice).
- SOW will call out pinning rules, acceptable model families, and permitted quantization modes — these affect capacity planning and therefore final unit price.
- We prefer to avoid long-term absolute guarantees on model-level QoE (quality regressions) — instead we provide regression monitoring and rollback windows in the Console.

I'll prepare redlined language for the SOW and a pricing appendix. Irene — can you share updated cost model with a 40/40/20 and the blended price points so procurement can compare Option A vs B side-by-side?

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Pricing & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
